$comment: Action precedence. Seven rows, five tie-break levels, two override kinds.
It is a DOCUMENT rather than Python for two reasons, and only the second is
about machinery. First: spec Q7 asks for precedence 'as something an
analyst can read and a regulator can be shown, rather than as ordering
logic', and a five-level tie-break written as nested ifs is precisely the
artefact doc 04 s6 says a reviewer cannot verify. Second: it is a
lexicographic argmax over fixed integer columns, which passes doc 08 s3.4's
generic-kernel test, so changing it costs no compile at all.
Spec s6.3 calls changing this 'a major event'. It is: two approvers, an
impact report and a board note. What it is not is a deployment.

stages.name: hard_block_floor
stages.rule: resolved action rank may not exceed hard_block_action_floor rank

stages.name: critical_binding
stages.rule: a fired rule with critical=true takes its action even where a less severe action would otherwise have won

stages.name: critical_allow_suppression
stages.rule: a fired critical rule with action=allow suppresses all non-critical firings in the families named by its critical_allow_families
stages.note: Suppressed firings are still RECORDED in live_fire_bits. They are removed from the resolution, not from the evidence.

stages.name: critical_collision
stages.rule: two or more fired critical rules asking for different actions: the more severe wins

stages.name: most_severe
stages.rule: the most severe action among the remaining firings

stages.name: tie_break
stages.note: rule_id last guarantees determinism; the three before it guarantee it is not arbitrary.
